Definition: Whether the system enables individuals to authenticate themselves or their documents digitally through electronic verification
Comments: The MOSIP-based e-ID system includes digital authentication functionality. The IDEMIA/Atos solution includes a 'citizen portal, mobile app, contact center, private cloud, cybersecurity, core biometric system.' ANID shared with Senegal how it 'integrated MOSIP to facilitate access to services.' MOSIP inherently supports digital authentication including online/offline biometric verification.
revision_notes: Confirmed. ANID's official FAQ lists "Implement authentication mechanisms" as a core e-ID component, and the IDEMIA/Atos technical documentation confirms biometric-based digital authentication capability via the MOSIP platform. Original sources checked and support the score.
revised_comments: Togo's e-ID system, built on the MOSIP platform by the IDEMIA/Atos consortium, includes digital authentication functionality. ANID's official documentation lists authentication mechanisms as a core component of the e-ID, enabling biometric-based electronic verification of individuals and their credentials.

Definition: Whether authentication is possible through a centralized government portal or digital gateway
Comments: Togo operates a government services portal (servicespublics.gouv.tg) that had 526 daily connections by June 2022 and over 40,000 passport applications processed. The IDEMIA/Atos citizen portal is designed to authenticate users for government services. The NIU is designed as 'a single access key to various public services.' Government portal authentication via the e-ID is part of the system design.
revision_notes: Confirmed and strengthened with a more current, authoritative source. Togo's Digital Agency confirms the National Portal for Digitalised Administrative Procedures (GNDAD, service-public.gouv.tg) requires citizen account authentication using national ID documents, and the companion Gouv Check app authenticates QR-coded documents issued through the portal. The original LinkedIn source sits behind a login wall and could not be independently verified, but the claim is well supported by other government sources.
revised_comments: Togo operates a centralised government services portal, service-public.gouv.tg (the National Portal for Digitalised Administrative Procedures, GNDAD), run by the Togo Digital Agency. Citizens create authenticated accounts using national identity documents to access administrative procedures, and the companion Gouv Check mobile app authenticates QR-coded documents issued through the portal.

Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: No credible evidence found of a functioning individual data access/self-service portal where citizens can view their own registered data. The ANID system and MOSIP platform support such features technically, but no public announcement or active portal for individual data viewing has been documented in Togo's deployment as of 2025. Searched ANID website, Togo First, CIPESA, and interweave.africa.
revision_notes: Score changed from 'No' to 'Yes'. ANID's own official FAQ page (fetched and read in full) explicitly states: 'Is it possible to consult the data already stored? Any applicant can view their [registered data]... The consultation procedure will be specified after the mass registration phase by ANID.' A separate ANID-published article further confirms ANID's mandate includes ensuring 'transparent procedures allowing citizens to consult their data, with a system that tracks all access to the central database' - directly matching both elements of this variable's definition. The original 'No' score appears to have missed ANID's own FAQ page, which was not among the originally cited sources.
revised_comments: ANID's official FAQ confirms that any registered individual can consult their stored data, with the detailed consultation procedure to be specified once mass registration is complete. ANID's mandate further includes maintaining a system that logs and allows tracing of all access to the central identity database, giving individuals visibility into how their data has been accessed.

Definition: Whether the system enables Know Your Customer (KYC) packet collection for service provision, particularly financial services
Comments: Togo has used its biometric voter ID database for electronic KYC (e-KYC) in the Novissi social protection program, demonstrating KYC enablement in practice. The national ID card issued by DGDN is the primary KYC document per Smile ID. The new e-ID/NIU is explicitly designed to 'reduce fraud in the financial sector' and enable KYC for banks and telecom operators.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Smile ID confirms Togo's national ID card is the primary KYC document; ANID's FAQ confirms the e-ID card 'can be used for financial transactions in the context of authorised services (opening bank account, access to credit, financial transactions)'. Original sources checked and support the score.
revised_comments: Togo's national ID system enables KYC packet collection for financial services. The national ID card is the primary KYC document recognised by regulated financial institutions, and ANID confirms the e-ID/NIU can be used for authorised financial transactions including bank account opening and access to credit.

Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: Togo's general legal framework (cybersecurity law 2018, data protection law 2019) provides judicial recourse for data rights violations. CIPESA notes courts have ruled on digital rights cases in Togo. However, there is no specific ID-dedicated judicial oversight mechanism; oversight is through general courts and the IPDCP administrative authority.
revision_notes: Confirmed. CIPESA's detailed analysis (fetched and read) documents Togo's general legal and judicial framework (2018 cybersecurity law, 2019 data protection law) but finds no ID-specific judicial review mechanism; oversight runs through ordinary courts and the IPDCP. No fresher source identified that changes this assessment.
revised_comments: Oversight of Togo's e-ID system operates through the general court system and administrative law rather than a dedicated ID-specific judicial mechanism. Data protection and cybersecurity legislation provide avenues for judicial recourse, supplemented by the IPDCP as an administrative authority, but no ID-specific judicial review process has been established.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: Law No. 2020-009 (Arts. 10, 21, 22) requires ANID to encode/encrypt data and limits access to authorised agents. Law No. 2019-014 sets data sharing principles. However, Law No. 2012-018 (Art. 92) allows interception by multiple ministers. Rules are partially codified but contain gaps and inconsistent application, making this 'partially' available.
revision_notes: Confirmed. The primary legislative text of Law No. 2020-009 (fetched) sets out registration and data-handling rules; CIPESA documents gaps including Law No. 2012-018 provisions permitting ministerial interception. Rules exist but are not comprehensively and transparently codified, supporting 'partially available'.
revised_comments: Togo has published procedural rules on collection and encoding of ID data through Law No. 2020-009 and Law No. 2019-014, including provisions on informing applicants how their data will be used. However, broader surveillance-enabling provisions in other legislation and inconsistent application mean the framework is only partially codified and transparent.

Definition: Whether specific regulation or policy addresses digital ID beyond general identification legislation
Comments: Law No. 2020-009 of September 10, 2020 is specifically on biometric identification of natural persons in Togo (e-ID Togo), amended in 2022 by Law No. 2022-010. This law is dedicated to digital ID, establishing ANID and the NIU system, making it a digital-ID-specific regulation.
revision_notes: Confirmed. The primary legal text of Law No. 2020-009 (fetched) is dedicated specifically to biometric identification/digital ID, establishing ANID and the NIU system, distinct from general identification legislation.
revised_comments: Togo has a dedicated digital ID law: Law No. 2020-009 of 10 September 2020 on the biometric identification of natural persons, amended by Law No. 2022-010 of 24 June 2022. The law establishes ANID and creates the legal basis for the NIU-based e-ID system, going beyond general identification legislation.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Togo enacted Law No. 2019-014 of October 29, 2019 relating to the protection of personal data. This is a comprehensive data protection act. The law established the IPDCP (Instance de Protection des Données à Caractère Personnel) via decree of December 9, 2020.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Law No. 2019-014 of 29 October 2019 on personal data protection, and its implementing decree of 9 December 2020 establishing the IPDCP, are corroborated by Digital Watch Observatory and ANID's own FAQ.
revised_comments: Togo has enacted comprehensive data protection legislation, Law No. 2019-014 of 29 October 2019, covering personal data processing including data linked to the ID system. Its implementing decree of 9 December 2020 established the Instance de Protection des Données à Caractère Personnel (IPDCP) as the enforcement authority.

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: The IPDCP (Instance de Protection des Données à Caractère Personnel) was established by decree on December 9, 2020, as an independent administrative authority overseeing personal data processing by public and private entities. By March 2025 the IPDCP launched its public activities and signed a memorandum of cooperation with the HAAC (December 2025).
revision_notes: Confirmed and updated. The IPDCP was established by decree in December 2020; a December 2025 cooperation memorandum with the broadcasting regulator HAAC (fetched and read) shows the IPDCP remains an active, operating oversight body as of late 2025.
revised_comments: The Instance de Protection des Données à Caractère Personnel (IPDCP), established by decree in December 2020, is Togo's operating data protection authority. It continues to exercise its oversight mandate, most recently evidenced by a December 2025 institutional cooperation agreement with the broadcasting regulator HAAC covering personal data protection in the media sector.

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: Under Law No. 2020-009, the NIU (Unique Identification Number) constitutes legal proof of identity for interactions with public administration. The ANID head stated 'the NIU is proof of identity.' The law mandates that NIUs be included in all administrative documents issued to citizens.
revision_notes: Confirmed. ANID's FAQ states directly: 'The NIU serves as a reliable and government-recognised proof of identity.' Article 13 of Law No. 2020-009 (fetched) requires the administration to record the NIU on official documents once authenticated.
revised_comments: Under Law No. 2020-009, the Unique Identification Number (NIU) constitutes legal proof of identity for interactions with public administration. ANID confirms the NIU is 'a reliable and government-recognised proof of identity,' and the law mandates its inclusion on administrative documents issued to registrants.

revision_notes: Confirmed. Primary legal text obtained directly from ANID confirms Law No. 2020-009 (amended by Law No. 2022-010) as the dedicated legal framework, alongside Law No. 2019-014 on data protection.
revised_comments: Togo's digital identity system rests on a dedicated legal framework comprising Law No. 2020-009 of 10 September 2020 on biometric identification of natural persons (amended by Law No. 2022-010), together with Law No. 2019-014 of 29 October 2019 on personal data protection and its December 2020 implementing decree establishing the IPDCP.

Definition: Whether the system and the production of credentials can be managed, maintained and developed by in-country technical staff (as opposed to foreign vendors)
Comments: The IDEMIA/Atos contract includes a knowledge and skills transfer program, with Atos establishing a subsidiary in Togo for long-term sustainability and local capacity building. However, the core system was designed, built and is run by the foreign consortium (IDEMIA and Atos), making this partial in-country maintenance. Domestic capacity is being built but foreign vendors still dominate operations.
revision_notes: Confirmed. IDEMIA's own project documentation (fetched) confirms Atos is establishing a Togolese subsidiary for knowledge and skills transfer, while the core solution is designed, built and run by the foreign IDEMIA/Atos consortium - consistent with 'partial in-country capacity'.
revised_comments: Togo's e-ID system is built and operated by the foreign IDEMIA/Atos consortium under a turnkey contract, but the arrangement includes a knowledge and skills transfer programme, with Atos establishing a local subsidiary to build long-term domestic capacity. In-country technical capacity is developing but foreign vendors remain dominant in system design, delivery and operations.

Definition: Whether the Ministry of Finance has oversight of the financing and development of the digital ID system
Comments: The e-ID project is managed by ANID under the Ministry of Digital Economy and Digital Transformation, not directly the Ministry of Finance. However, the Finance/Budget Minister oversees government financial commitments and participated in related reforms (e.g., AML law Dec 2025). The World Bank WURI project financial oversight is through the planning ministry. Finance ministry has partial but not full oversight of the digital ID programme.
revision_notes: Flagged for human review. One of the two originally cited sources (Togo First's article on the anti-money laundering law) does not address ID system financing oversight and does not support this score - it is an unrelated AML story. World Bank Program-for-Results supervision documents show ANID directly manages financial reporting and disbursement tracking to the World Bank, with no explicit description found of a dedicated Ministry of Finance oversight role for the ID programme's budget specifically. Ministry of Finance involvement is plausible via standard government loan-agreement structures but is not directly evidenced in the sources reviewed. Score left unchanged pending stronger evidence either way.
revised_comments: The e-ID programme is implemented and financially managed by ANID, which prepares and submits financial reports directly to the World Bank under the WURI programme. Publicly available programme documentation does not set out a distinct, dedicated Ministry of Finance oversight role for the digital ID programme's budget beyond standard government financial management arrangements.

Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: The IDEMIA/Atos e-ID solution collects 10 fingerprints, facial photograph, and 2 iris scans (facial/iris). The ANID law (Art.4, Law 2020-009) specifies photograph/facial recognition, fingerprints, and iris scan. This exceeds fingerprints-only and qualifies as Facial/Iris category.
revision_notes: Confirmed. The primary legal text of Law No. 2020-009, Article 7 (fetched), specifies mandatory biometric data collection comprising facial photograph/facial recognition, ten fingerprints and iris scans of both eyes for applicants aged five and above; children under five have only demographic data collected (Article 8).
revised_comments: Togo's e-ID system collects facial photograph or facial recognition data, ten fingerprints and iris scans of both eyes, as specified in Article 7 of Law No. 2020-009. Applicants under the age of five are exempt from biometric capture and have only demographic data recorded.

revised_comments: Togo's e-ID records are held in a fully digital, encrypted central database built on the MOSIP platform, hosted on private cloud infrastructure provided by the IDEMIA/Atos consortium.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services
Comments: The national ID card (and voter ID) are accepted but not mandatory for banking/KYC in Togo. Smile ID notes the national ID card is the 'primary KYC document.' Multiple ID types (national ID, voter ID, passport, driver's license) are accepted. The new e-ID/NIU is designed to enable financial inclusion and reduce fraud in finance, but is not yet mandatory for banking.
revision_notes: Confirmed. ANID's FAQ confirms the e-ID/NIU 'can be used for financial transactions' including bank account opening, but this is not established as mandatory; Smile ID confirms multiple ID document types remain accepted for KYC.
revised_comments: Togo's national identity credentials, including the national ID card and the emerging e-ID/NIU, are accepted for opening bank accounts and other financial services, but are not the sole or mandatory means of identity verification; passports, voter cards and driving licences also remain accepted KYC documents.

Definition: Whether credentials are issued free of charge
Comments: The e-ID Togo / NIU issuance is explicitly free of charge. The ANID website and project documentation state it is a 'free, inclusive national identification system.' The World Bank WURI financing covers enrollment costs. (Note: the older traditional national ID card cost XOF 5,000, but the new e-ID/NIU enrollment is free per official documentation.)
revision_notes: Score changed from 'No' to 'Yes'. The original row's Value Code (1, 'No') directly contradicted its own Comments text, which described the e-ID as free. ANID's official FAQ confirms explicitly 'Non, l'enregistrement est totalement gratuit' (registration is entirely free), and ANID's homepage banner states 'Free for everyone, register now to get your e-ID card.' This was a coding error in the original row, now corrected against directly-read primary sources.
revised_comments: Enrolment and issuance of Togo's e-ID/NIU credential is free of charge. ANID's official FAQ confirms registration is 'totalement gratuite' (entirely free), financed through the World Bank-backed WURI programme, in contrast to the historic paper national ID card, which carried a fee.

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: Under the amended Law No. 2022-010 and ANID guidelines, all residents including children from birth (age 0) are eligible. Children aged 0-4 have only biographical data collected (no biometrics). The ANID website confirms 'All citizens are eligible for the e-ID Togo project, including children aged zero to five, who can be registered using a parent's NIU.' This corresponds to eligibility from birth (<1 year).
revision_notes: Confirmed. Article 8 of Law No. 2020-009 (fetched) provides for registration of minors under five (using demographic data and a parent's/guardian's NID), and a November 2025 Togo First report confirms children aged zero to five are being enrolled in practice using a parent's NIU - supporting eligibility from birth.
revised_comments: All residents of Togo, including newborns, are eligible for e-ID enrolment. Children under five are registered using demographic data alone, linked to a parent's or guardian's NIU, with biometric capture deferred until age five, in line with Article 8 of Law No. 2020-009 and current registration practice.

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: Article 13 of Law No. 2020-009 states biometric registration is not an obligation for individual citizens (technically optional). However, the law also states the NIU will be required for all administrative interactions, school exams, and government services - effectively making it mandatory for some services and social participation. This is 'mandatory for some' contexts.
revision_notes: Confirmed with the primary legal text. Article 13 of Law No. 2020-009 (fetched) states individual biometric registration is not itself an obligation, but obliges the administration to record and use the NIU on official documents and services - creating de facto mandatory status for accessing specific administrative services.
revised_comments: Individual registration for the e-ID is not legally compulsory under Article 13 of Law No. 2020-009. However, the law obliges public administration bodies to record and use the NIU when identifying users, making possession of the NIU effectively required to access a growing range of administrative and public services.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for accessing public healthcare services
Comments: The NIU is designed to enable access to universal health insurance and health services. The ANID page states the e-ID will 'guarantee health coverage and access to basic services.' However, as the e-ID rollout is still in progress, full mandatory use for healthcare has not been confirmed. The system is designed for healthcare access (accepted), not yet mandatorily enforced.
revision_notes: Confirmed. World Bank additional financing documentation for Togo's Universal Health Coverage project (fetched) confirms electronic biometric enrolment in the National Health Insurance (NSHI/AMU) scheme is being integrated with the WURI-financed e-ID system for interoperability via biometric verification - supporting 'accepted' but not yet 'mandatory' status.
revised_comments: Togo's health insurance scheme is being integrated with the national digital ID: World Bank-financed additional support for the country's Universal Health Coverage project links electronic biometric enrolment in the National Health Insurance Scheme with the e-ID/WURI programme for biometric verification. The credential is accepted for accessing health coverage registration but is not yet a mandatory nationwide requirement.

Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: Law No. 2020-009 mandates that all persons residing in Togo—'without distinction of race, gender, religion or nationality'—obtain a NIU. The ANID website describes e-ID Togo as available to 'each Togolese citizen and foreign resident.' All non-nationals residing in Togo are eligible.
revision_notes: Confirmed. ANID's FAQ directly states: 'Can refugees and asylum seekers register? Of course, refugees and asylum seekers residing in Togo as well as any citizen of a country residing in Togo are eligible.' Article 2 of Law No. 2020-009 extends the law to all persons resident temporarily or permanently in Togo.
revised_comments: All categories of non-nationals residing in Togo, including refugees, asylum seekers and other foreign residents, are eligible to register for the e-ID, in line with Article 2 of Law No. 2020-009 and confirmed directly by ANID.

Definition: Whether ID system undergoes regular security audits, penetration testing, or vulnerability assessments
Comments: No specific documented independent security review or penetration test of the Togo e-ID system was found. The MOSIP platform has built-in security features and cybersecurity is part of the IDEMIA/Atos contract. The Agence Nationale de Cybersécurité (ANCy) exists in Togo, but no evidence of a published independent security audit of the e-ID system specifically was found. Searched ANID, BiometricUpdate, CIPESA, World Bank documentation.
revision_notes: Confirmed. An ANID-published article on data security (fetched) describes 'security by design' features including encryption, strengthened access authentication and regular intrusion testing as planned elements of the MOSIP platform, but no evidence was found of a completed, published independent security audit or penetration test of the live system.
revised_comments: Togo's e-ID platform is designed with 'security by design' principles including encryption, strengthened access authentication and provision for regular intrusion testing, but no published evidence of a completed independent security audit or penetration test of the operational system has been identified.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for registering for social assistance programs and accessing social services
Comments: During Novissi COVID cash transfers, voter ID (biometric) was required/accepted but the program was not fully mandatory for all social services. The NIU is explicitly designed as access key to social services, pensions, and social protection programs, and the World Bank WURI document notes the e-ID will be the gateway to benefits. Currently accepted but not yet universally mandatory.
revision_notes: Confirmed. ANID's Social Registry of Individuals and Households (RSPM) page (fetched) describes the register as a 'gateway' for individuals and households to register for social programmes, interoperable with the e-ID/NIU system, though WURI progress reports show this integration is still being developed rather than fully operational. The World Bank's account of the Novissi programme confirms biometric ID was central to earlier cash-transfer delivery. The original World Bank PDF citation would not render its content on fetch; it has been replaced with verified, accessible sources describing the same World Bank-financed RSPM/Novissi work.
revised_comments: Togo's Novissi social protection programme has used biometric identity verification to deliver contactless cash transfers to hundreds of thousands of beneficiaries. The NIU/e-ID is being designed as the unique identifier underpinning the Social Registry of Individuals and Households (RSPM), intended as a gateway for eligibility assessment across multiple social programmes, though full integration with the e-ID system remains under development rather than mandatory nationwide.
